title: OSS survey: checkpointing, time-travel & versioned data stores for per-agent rollback
outcome: Know whether any existing substrate can revert one author's changes while keeping others' later dependent work, and pick our storage substrate
acceptance: ≥5 tools surveyed with repo/docs URLs (e.g. LangGraph checkpointer/time-travel, Dolt, lakeFS, Git, Temporal, FS/VM snapshots)
Table: tool × rollback granularity (whole state / branch / per-author / per-row) × keeps-others'-work? × conflict handling × Python/offline usable
A small tested-or-documented example (from docs or a local run) of reverting one author's commit in the best candidate
'Implications for our design' section recommending a substrate for the prototype's Recovery component
summary:
Surveyed 7 substrates (LangGraph, Temporal, Replit snapshots, DeltaBox, Git, Dolt, lakeFS); H6 holds: checkpoint/time-travel tools restore whole state and drop others' work.
Correction: commit-graph stores (Dolt, Git, lakeFS) have 'revert one commit, keep later commits'; per-author undo = revert all commits by author X.
Local Git run: independent non-adjacent edit reverts cleanly; dependent edit conflicts. Git conflicts on adjacent lines, Dolt on same cell.
Surprise: lakeFS is BSL 1.1 and object-level; none record reads, so dependency tracking must be our own layer.
Verdict: Dolt (row-level revert, SQL, Apache-2.0) for shared state, Git fallback, plus own provenance graph. Dolt not run locally (binary not executed); verified from tests/docs only.
review:
[anaya · done] DONE. All 4 criteria met (7 substrates, granularity/keeps-work/conflict/offline table, local Git run + Dolt engine-test example, substrate recommendation). Strongest finding: commit-graph stores already do 'revert one commit, keep later ones'; what none has is READ tracking, so dependency is our layer. H6 CONFIRMED for checkpoint/time-travel tools and REFINED for commit-graph stores - strong support for the 'dependency problem, not snapshot problem' thesis.
Spot-check: Dolt docs confirm DOLT_REVERT --author and that DOLT_CHERRY_PICK 'preserves the original commit's author identity'; re-check the longer DOLT_REVERT quote, docs I saw say 'Reverts the changes introduced in a commit, or set of commits.'
Recommendation (Dolt) is NOT yet accepted: Dolt was not run, and an external Go binary + MySQL client sits outside CHARTER's stdlib/pydantic/cryptography/networkx/pytest list. Decide Dolt vs own row-versioned store at Call #1/ADR.
